trades.thesis: Rate markets now price a possible December Fed hike after the hot CPI, but QQQ is roughly flat on the week. Its long-duration tech names are also exposed to the AI leadership turmoil ('Nasdaq futures drop as Nvidia leads decline in AI-related shares').

The Huang scandal has revived China chip-curb pressure ahead of the Trump-Xi summit, and the US is widening AI export controls to seven nations and pressing South Korea. Chip-equipment makers with large China revenue are the most direct target, and LRCX is up 6.5% in 5 days on the rotation away from Nvidia.

Small caps are the most rate-sensitive part of the equity market because they carry more floating-rate debt and are more exposed to credit. Yet IWM is up 0.3% over five days while hike odds have jumped. I prefer it over SPY or QQQ as the single equity short on the rates theme.

This is the cleanest way to trade the hawkish repricing. 'Dollar firms as hot inflation, hawkish Fed talk lift rate-hike bets', and talk of a possible 50bp hike widens the US rate advantage over other countries. It is only up 0.5% over five days, so most of the move probably hasn't happened yet.

AMD rose 8.9% as traders rotated out of NVDA after the scandal. But the bill Congress is pushing would block all AI chip exports to China, which hits AMD's China accelerator sales too. The rally ignores that shared risk, and the hawkish Fed adds pressure on high-valuation semis.

The Fed has made its first hike since 2023, and Waller is putting a 50bp December move on the table. Yet the dollar is flat over 5 days, so the widening rate gap hasn't been priced. Falling oil also eases a source of pressure on the dollar's terms of trade without hurting the US rate advantage.

Nvidia has opened an internal investigation into Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, and the BBC frames it as a national security issue. That creates real risk of a CEO change and more Washington scrutiny of China chip sales, on top of hawkish rates weighing on long-duration tech.

Hot October jobs data (+165k, unemployment down to 4.1%) pushed December hike odds past 65%, yet TLT is flat over 5 days (+0.1%). Long bonds look under-priced for a hawkish Fed, and a firm CPI print would close that gap.
